newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian warship brings out Albania evacuees.
newsitem.headline: Italian warship brings out Albania evacuees.

text.p: An Italian warship brought more than 800 foreigners and Albanians to safety on Friday after a military evacuation from Albania's lawlessness.
The amphibious assault ship San Giusto, crammed with 868 refugees from 31 nations, docked in the southeastern Italian port of Brindisi after more than a day at sea.
Nearly half its passengers, 432, were Albanians, 80 of them without proper papers, Italian navy and port officials said.

The rest included 208 Italians, 64 British, 64 Americans, 50 Croats, 16 Germans, 11 Canadians 10 Dutch and small groups or individuals foreigners plucked by helicopters from the capital Tirana or lifted by landing craft from the port of Durres.
Some of the passengers, exhausted but relieved, said their ordeal had lasted 36 hours from the moment they got the word they would be evacuated.
"No one has returned injured. Everyone travelled well though a few of the Italians were a bit nervous, which is understandable," the ship's captain, Ernesto Pullano, told reporters.
Several Britons off the ship complained that crack Italian soldiers sent to get them had abandoned them overnight on a freezing beach in Durres at the mercy of armed Albanians.
They said the Italians had shot dead one Albanian man and wounded four in a gun battle on Thursday night before retreating out to sea for several hours.
But other passengers had only praise for the operation.
"It was all really well organised. We had no problems. We were put on the boat and it was perfect," a Canadian woman, who would not give her name, told Reuters.
Diplomats awaiting the vessel said arrangements were being made to get the foreigners home.
Britain was providing a charter flight to London and Italy's airline Alitalia said it was sending a plane to Brindisi to bring Italians and other nationals to Rome.

The evacuees were rescued from the chaos and anarchy spreading through Albania in an Italian military mission launched on Thursday and concluded earlier on Friday. It was not immediately clear why so many Albanians were on board.

Brindisi, southeast Italy's main port, also saw an influx on Friday of scores of Albanians who fled the chaos in their country in a flotilla of creaking boats, many of them navy craft carrying deserting servicemen and civilians.
At least 13 Albanian navy boats were in the port on Friday, including one that docked just before midnight with between 130 and 150 civilians, including several children.
